title: run pool --jobs N runs the pool's paid runs in parallel within a --max-usd cap and keeps one record date
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run pool --jobs N runs up to N claude -p runs at once (fresh shape: one run per pool row, cell and rep; session shape: one session per group, its six questions in order inside it), writes the same rows in the same order as --jobs 1 whatever order the runs finish in, and stamps every row with the record date the run started on, so a run that crosses midnight is one record; --max-usd X stops launching new runs once the spend of finished runs reaches X, lets the runs in flight finish, records a spend_stopped row naming the runs not started, and exits 1; --dry-run prints the run count and an estimate of the spend from the per-model prices of bench_core; a test runs a fake runner with out-of-order completion at --jobs 3 and checks the rows equal --jobs 1's, one record date across a planted date change, and the stop at the cap; kb/_self/tools.md and kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md name the flags
